entries.clue: Small accident spoiled most of pie and mash (6)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: spoiled letters are ruined and rearranged
indicatorNotes.most of: keep all but the last letter of 'pie'

annotation.surface: A cook's small kitchen disaster ruins the pie and mash.
annotation.walkthrough: Pie and mash is a traditional London working-class dish; here both words are just raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mishap is by nature minor, so 'small' is part of the definition rather than padding.

entries.clue: Working demonstration’s enthralling Queen (7)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: to enthral is to hold captive, so MARCH holds ON inside it

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A protest march captivates the reigning Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like an adjective describing the demonstration, but it is its own piece, and the capital Q on Queen is only there to hide the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a reigning queen is one kind of monarch.

entries.clue: Vowed to be tender, protecting wife (5)

indicatorNotes.protecting: SORE wraps around W as if shielding it

blocks.note: tender as in painful to the touch

annotation.surface: A husband promises to be gentle and look after his wife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as loving in the surface; it is the sore, painful sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Swore is the past tense of swear, to vow.

entries.clue: Vie and cheat briefly, desperate to win (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: drop the last letter of 'cheat'
indicatorNotes.desperate: desperate as in frantic and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A competitor so desperate to win that they will compete and cheat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' seems to describe the competitor's mood but works on the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of gaining something by effort, as in winning or achieving recognition.

entries.clue: Cheers Celtic eluding the Spanish strategy (6)

indicatorNotes.eluding: to elude is to escape, so EL escapes from CELTIC

blocks.note: CELTIC with EL, Spanish for 'the', taken out

annotation.surface: Fans cheer as Celtic, the Glasgow football club, get past the Spanish side with clever strategy.
annotation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks; Celtic is a Scottish football club, a word here only for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: strictly a tactic is one move within a larger strategy, but everyday use treats them alike.

entries.clue: Clever you, finally infiltrating state organisation (6)

indicatorNotes.infiltrating: U gets inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.organisation: the letters of STATE are organised, rearranged

annotation.surface: Praise for a spy clever enough to infiltrate a state organisation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State organisation' looks like a government body; 'organisation' is actually the instruction to rearrange STATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, leaning towards the shrewd, sharp-witted side of clever.

entries.clue: Short article on outbreak available for debate (6,3)

indicatorNotes.Short: cut the last letter from THE

blocks.note: THE, the definite article, cut short
as a new book or record is out

annotation.surface: A brief newspaper piece about a disease outbreak is up for public debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak' suggests an epidemic, but a skin rash is an outbreak too.
annotation.definitionFit: To thrash out an issue is to debate it until settled.

entries.clue: Steering boat to take in capital of Antigua’s tempting (7)

indicatorNotes.to take in: to take something in is to admit it inside, as a house takes in a lodger, so one piece goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.capital of: the capital, first, letter of Antigua

blocks.note: the cox steers a rowing boat

annotation.surface: Sailing a boat to call at St John's, Antigua's capital, sounds tempting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Antigua' wants to be St John's; it is simply its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Coaxing is gently tempting someone into something.

entries.clue: Rang computer department to resign; succeeded and put end to dispute (6,2,5)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in family trees

annotation.surface: Someone phoned IT to resign, got their way, and ended the row.
annotation.walkthrough: The semicolon splits the surface in two, but everything before 'and' is one run of wordplay. S for succeeded comes from genealogy, where 's.' marks who succeeded whom.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: calling it quits means agreeing to stop, here stopping a quarrel.

entries.clue: Cancel posh party after first night (4)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following in sequence, so the party is written following the first of night

annotation.surface: Calling off a smart party following a theatre's opening night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First night' looks like a premiere; it only supplies N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean reversing an action so it no longer takes effect.

entries.clue: Something that beats rest for pain? (10)

annotation.surface: A riddle: what cures pain better than rest?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beats' seems to mean surpasses; it is the heartbeat.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: grief over lost love is one particular kind of pain.

entries.clue: Cool-sounding decorative strip around room (6)

indicatorNotes.sounding: the answer sounds like a word meaning cool

annotation.surface: A trendy decorative border around a room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cool-sounding' reads as trendy-looking; it asks for a word said like FREEZE.
annotation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorative band along the top of a wall.

entries.clue: Gives away rejected lager and Stella with a third off (4,4)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected things are turned back, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.with a third off: remove a third of STELLA's six letters, the last two

annotation.surface: A drinker turns down lager and gives away most of their Stella Artois.
annotation.walkthrough: Stella is Stella Artois, a lager sold widely in Britain; both brands are just letters here. Reverse PILSSTEL to get LETSSLIP.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: revealing a secret by accident, which is giving it away.

entries.clue: Livestock managers initially prefer to split female flocks (9)

indicatorNotes.to split: P splits SHE from HERDS by going between them

blocks.note: gathers in a group, as a verb

annotation.surface: Farmers would rather separate the female animals in their flocks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flocks' reads as a noun, groups of sheep; it is the verb, gathers together, and 'female' is a pronoun, not an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: shepherds are the people who tend and manage sheep, which are livestock.

entries.clue: Went along with parent worried about daughter (9)

indicatorNotes.worried: a worried thing is disturbed, so its letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone tagged along with a parent who was anxious about their daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the link to daughter; it is RE, a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: To partner someone is to go along with them as a companion.

entries.clue: Hum piano tune dropping intro (4)

indicatorNotes.dropping intro: lose the introduction, the first letter, of SONG

annotation.surface: Humming a piano melody but skipping its opening bars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hum' is not singing: it is British slang for a bad smell, as is pong.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang both a hum and a pong are an unpleasant smell.

entries.clue: Horse requires time and money to be turned around (4)

indicatorNotes.to be turned around: the letters are turned to run the other way

annotation.surface: Turning a horse around takes time and money.
annotation.walkthrough: ERA plus M runs backwards to give MARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is specifically a female horse, so 'horse' is the broader class.

entries.clue: Mum and John played golf game (7)

indicatorNotes.played: played around with, so the letters of JOHN are rearranged

blocks.note: G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Mother and John had a round of golf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Golf game' looks like one phrase; golf is only G, and 'game' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is a Chinese tile game, one example of a game.

entries.clue: Required by law to have artwork contracted by politician (9)

indicatorNotes.contracted: shortened: drop the last letter of STATUE

blocks.note: a member of the British Conservative Party

annotation.surface: A politician has been legally obliged to commission a public artwork.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests a commission, but it means shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a statute is a written law, and the adjective describes what such a law demands.

entries.clue: High wind ripped a door half off (7)

indicatorNotes.half off: remove half of DOOR, its second half

annotation.surface: A gale tore a door half off its hinges.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half off' reads as the door hanging loose; it removes half the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a violently rotating column of air is an extreme example of a high wind.

entries.clue: Book substitute (7)

blocks.note: a verb here, as in booking a table or seat
a noun: a player on the bench

annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns; 'Book' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb meaning to arrange in advance, and the noun for a squad player kept back to come on later.

entries.clue: Some lovely cheese and fruit (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: the answer is some of the letters in the next words

annotation.surface: A pleasant snack of cheese and fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' sits at the far end with 'and' as the joint, so the whole of 'lovely cheese' is the place to look.
annotation.definitionFit: A lychee is a small sweet tropical fruit.

entries.clue: You shouldn’t have tissue stuffed in to back of bureau (5,3)

blocks.note: a handkerchief, or a paper tissue

annotation.surface: A scolding: you shouldn't have crammed tissues into the back of the desk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' reads as a rebuke, but it is what people say on getting a gift. A bureau is a writing desk.
annotation.definitionFit: 'You shouldn't have' is a polite way to say thank you for a present.

entries.clue: Say no to waste (6)

annotation.walkthrough: The two senses share a spelling but are pronounced differently, stress on the second syllable for the verb and the first for the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb for declining, and the noun for household rubbish.

entries.clue: Husband invested in elaborate gift box (5)

indicatorNotes.invested in: H is put inside, as money is put into a venture
indicatorNotes.elaborate: elaborate means intricately worked, so the letters of GIFT are reworked

annotation.surface: A husband spent money on a fancy gift box.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gift box' looks like a noun phrase; 'box' is the verb, to fight.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: boxing is fighting with the fists, and both work as verbs.

entries.clue: Act as mother in retrospective work with university theatre cast (4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.retrospective: looking backwards, so OP runs the other way
indicatorNotes.cast: the letters of THEATRE are cast, thrown into a new shape

annotation.surface: An actor plays a mother in a retrospective show by a university theatre company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre cast' looks like the actors; 'cast' is the instruction to rearrange. In Britain, asking 'shall I be mother?' means offering to pour the tea.
annotation.definitionFit: To 'be mother' is British idiom for pouring the tea for everyone.

entries.clue: Virus: retired man’s energy beginning to go (4)

indicatorNotes.retired: retired as in withdrawn, drawn back, so MR runs backwards

annotation.surface: A retired man, sick with a virus, has no energy to go out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests a pensioner; it only reverses MR.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, everyday synonym: any disease-causing microbe, a virus included, is popularly called a germ.

entries.clue: Notice packing goods evenly tests clever little appliance (6)

indicatorNotes.packing: packing means holding inside, as a case packs clothes, so the notice goes inside the goods

annotation.surface: An advert for goods boasts that a clever little gadget passes every test.
annotation.walkthrough: G is the standard abbreviation for good, so 'goods' is read as two of them, GG.
annotation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small, ingenious device.

entries.clue: Nerve of boy messing up toilet I scrubbed! (6)

indicatorNotes.messing up: the letters of TOLET are messed up, rearranged
indicatorNotes.scrubbed: scrubbed as in cancelled, so I is removed

annotation.surface: A boy has the nerve to make a mess of the toilet just cleaned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrubbed' pretends to be cleaning; it means deleted. Bottle is British slang for courage.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang, bottle is nerve or courage.
